author: review-planner
rationale: code-quality-reviewer: production control-flow change (clamping) warrants a readability/style pass; test-reviewer: new parameterized tests cover the changed branch (page=0,-3) and need edge-case/pyramid review; security-reviewer excluded: page is a bounded int param clamped server-side, no new trust-boundary, auth, or dependency surface; doc-reviewer excluded: no docs/ brief describes pagination behavior and no documented contract changed.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: Both controllers clamp the requested page at the HTTP boundary with the same small, readable pattern (private FIRST_PAGE constant + Math.max), mirroring the project's documented convention of declaring pagination details independently per controller (docs/system-design.md)
requestedPage is a distinct, descriptively named local var, not reusing the raw @RequestParam page value for downstream logic, which keeps the clamp visible at the call site
Explanatory comment states the 1-based rationale inline where the clamp happens
checkFormat passes cleanly; no style, naming, or duplication concerns worth raising for a two-call-site fix this size

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Confirming, not disputing: the new test names theOwnerSearchShouldTreatAPageBelowOneAsTheFirstPage / theVetDirectoryShouldTreatAPageBelowOneAsTheFirstPage correctly follow the BDD school per the brief's 2026-07-31 cutover, even though every neighboring test in both files still uses the pre-cutover method-name style. No brief defect found; recording this so a future reviewer does not mistake the stylistic divergence within the file for an inconsistency.

approved_aspects: Both @ParameterizedTest cases use @ValueSource(ints = {0, -3}), reproducing exactly the two symptom values named in the bug report (page=0 and page=-3), giving each parameter combination independent meaning without invented data

Tests assert status 200 + the normal list view + model attribute currentPage == 1, which is the value the fix's Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) clamp produces before the code path that previously threw IllegalArgumentException from PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) — a pre-fix run of these tests would fail with a 5xx/error view, so the test is a true regression guard, not a tautology

Swept the changed production surface (PageRequest.of call sites) for other instances of the unclamped-page defect class: only OwnerController and VetController construct PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...), and both are covered by the new parameterized tests — no missed instance

New test bodies are four-phase (arrange/act/assert separated by blank lines, no phase comments), reuse the file's existing george()/james()/helen() factories and mocking idiom (given/when matching the adjacent test in each file), and the one added comment explains a non-obvious setup choice (why two owners are stubbed) rather than narrating code
Mocking stays within the brief's policy: MockMvc is the sanctioned transport boundary mock, and the stubbed repository return values are real PageImpl/Owner/Vet value objects, not further mocks
./gradlew test passes cleanly for both modified test classes; no coverage regression on the changed branches

author: change-grader
summary: clamp below-one page requests to the first page

blast_radius.note: Four files in one module, 17 production lines across two request-handling methods, 10 hunks, no sensitive paths, no config, schema, dependency, or binary changes; each edit is local to the method it sits in.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk: the clamp is Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) applied to both consumers of the value in each method (the repository page request and the currentPage model attribute), and Math.max is the identity for page >= 1, so no existing path changes; grep confirms no other page consumer in either method and the JSON /vets endpoint is untouched.

test_adequacy.note: The new parameterized cases are genuine regression guards - before the fix PageRequest.of(-1, 5) threw, so status 200 plus currentPage 1 could not have passed - but no test in either file exercises a page above 1, so replacing the clamp with a constant first page would leave the whole suite green; one case at page=2 asserting currentPage is 2 closes the gap.

reviewer_hedging.note: Both dispatched reviewers approved; code-quality with an empty findings list, test-reviewer with a single clarify finding that self-describes as confirming rather than disputing (the BDD test names diverge from their neighbors by the brief's own naming cutover). Security- and doc-reviewer are null because the review plan explicitly scoped them out with a stated rationale, which is expected silence, not a hedge.

scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions, consultations, and build retries; the diff is confined to the two triaged call sites. VetController and /vets.html belong to a vet requirement while the slice is filed under REQ-OWN-002, but the review plan recorded both files up front as one defect class, so this is a deliberate sweep rather than drift. The clamp policy - a silent 200 at the non-canonical URL rather than a 400 or a redirect to page=1 - is a user-visible choice the PRD does not record.

rationale: The fix itself reads clean: Math.max at both call sites, identity for valid pages, no other consumer of the value. The gap is test evidence - nothing pins that page=2 still reaches page 2, so a pin-to-first-page clamp would also pass green. Add one page=2 case.
